pr-check.does: Check a PR body file, or - for stdin, for its shape, mentions, bare references and em dashes, with pr-check <file> [--json].

pr-night.does: Say as JSON whether steps that notify people wait for the morning.

does: Opens and updates pull requests the way each repo's guide asks. Steps that notify people wait for the user's order.

children.does: How new PRs open when the repo's guide and the user say nothing: as drafts or ready for review.
Hours in which steps that notify people wait for the morning, such as 22:00-07:00, in away_guard's time zone or the system's. Empty means none.
The sections of the hub-pr skill.
Read the repo's contributing guide, PR template and agent instructions first, and follow them.
New or changed words users read go in their own small PR, which merges before the logic.
One feature per PR, with its first real use, and a split proposed before a PR grows too large.
A fixed body shape, written whole again on each update and checked with pr-check.
Before each push, a few fat behaviour scenarios and the repo's smoke run pass, and the body says how it was tested and what was not.
The user's writing skill runs on the title, the body and each commit message.
New PRs open the way pr.open_as says, unless the repo's guide or the user asks otherwise.
A change to env keys, secrets or settings is named first, before the merge and again when it lands.
Steps that notify people wait during pr.quiet_hours, unless the user says to send them now.
Another PR skill that is on does its own step, and the three PR rules still hold.
Replaced work is closed with a link to the new work, and its branch is kept.
